'''''Foskeia''''' is an extinct genus of [[rhabdodontomorph]] [[ornithopod]] dinosaurs known from the [[Early Cretaceous]] ([[Barremian]] to [[Aptian]] ages) [[Castrillo de la Reina Formation]] of Spain. The genus contains a [[monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Foskeia pelendonum''''', known from fossils of multiple individuals of different ontogenetic stages. Before its formal description, it had been nicknamed the "Vegagete ornithopod."<ref name="Foskeia">{{Cite journal |last1=Dieudonné |first1=Paul‐Emile |last2=Becerra |first2=Marcos Gabriel |last3=Zanesco |first3=Tábata |last4=Tortosa |first4=Thierry |last5=Cruzado‐Caballero |first5=Penélope |last6=Stein |first6=Koen |last7=Torcida Fernández‐Baldor |first7=Fidel |date=2026-02-01 |title=''Foskeia pelendonum'', a new rhabdodontomorph from the Lower Cretaceous of Salas de los Infantes (Burgos Province, Spain), and a new phylogeny of ornithischian dinosaurs |journal=[[Papers in Palaeontology]] |language=en |volume=12 |issue=1 |doi=10.1002/spp2.70057 |issn=2056-2799}}</ref>

== History of discovery ==
In 2016, Dieudonné et al. reported the discovery of at least five individuals of a gracile, small-bodied ornithopod (approximately {{cvt|0.5|m|ft}} long), representing several distinct ontogenetic stages. Despite the abundance of material, the describers refrained from assigning a [[binomial name]] to it, instead referring to it as the "Vegagete ornithopod," after the locality where the fossils were found. This locality is part of the [[Castrillo de la Reina Formation]] (Cameros Basin) in [[Burgos Province]], Spain, a site known for its rich diversity of Early Cretaceous dinosaur remains.<ref name="PD16">{{cite journal | title=An Unexpected Early Rhabdodontid from Europe (Lower Cretaceous of Salas de los Infantes, Burgos Province, Spain) and a Re-Examination of Basal Iguanodontian Relationships | last1 = Dieudonné | first1 = Paul-Emile |last2=Tortosa| first2 = Thierry |last3 = Fernández-Baldor | first3 = Fidel Torcida |last4 =Canudo |first4 =José Ignacio | last5 = Díaz-Martínez | first5 = Ignacio | journal=PLOS ONE | year=2016 | volume=11 | issue=6 | doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0156251| pmc=4917257 | pmid=27333279 | article-number=e0156251| bibcode = 2016PLoSO..1156251D | doi-access=free }}</ref>  

[[File:3D skull reconstruction of Foskeia pelendonum.jpg|thumb|left|3D skull reconstruction]]
The discovery of new cranial elements in subsequent fieldwork and assessment of this material via [[μCT]] scanning allowed the remains to be formally described as a new genus and species of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod in 2026.<ref name="Foskeia" /> The [[genus|generic name]], ''Foskeia'', is derived from the [[Ancient Greek]] words {{lang|grc|[[wiktionary:φῶς|φῶς]]}} (light) and {{lang|grc|[[wiktionary:βόσκειν|βόσκειν]]}} (to forage), referring to its small size and presumed herbivorous habits. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''pelendonum'', is a reference to the [[Pellendones|Pelendones]], a [[Celtiberians|Celtiberian]] tribe from the Fuentes de Duero, near the type locality.<ref name="Phys">{{cite web|author=Free University of Brussels|url=https://phys.org/news/2026-01-tiny-dinosaur-foskeia-pelendonum-evolutionary.html|title=Tiny new dinosaur ''Foskeia pelendonum'' fills in an evolutionary gap|publisher=Phys.org|access-date=2026-02-02}}</ref>

== Paleobiology ==  
Analysis of the limb bones performed by Dieudonné et al. (2023) revealed that ''Foskeia'' juveniles began life as [[quadrupedal]] animals. However, at an early stage in their ontogeny, they transitioned to [[bipedalism]]. Histological analysis of the limb bones further revealed that the largest known individual of ''Foskeia'' represents a late [[subadult]], which supports the interpretation that the species was among the smallest ornithopods. The study showed that the ontogenetic pathway of ''Foskeia'' involved significant skeletal changes, with muscle attachment marks observed on the [[femora]] and [[tibiae]] indicating the gradual development of a more dynamic and efficient locomotor system as the animal matured. This postural transition is consistent with other early rhabdodontomorphs.<ref name="Dieudonné2022">{{cite journal|vauthors=Dieudonné PE, Torcida Fernández-Baldor F, Stein K |title=Histogenesis and growth dynamics of the tiny Vegagete rhabdodontomorph hindlimb ([[Ornithischia]], [[Ornithopoda]]): paleoecological and evolutionary implications |journal=[[Cretaceous Research]] |year=2022 |volume=141 |article-number=105342 |doi=10.1016/j.cretres.2022.105342 |s2cid=251984848 |hdl=11336/227344 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

== Classification ==
[[File:Foskeia pelendonum.png|thumb|Speculative [[paleoart|life restoration]]]]
When it was first described by Dieudonné and colleagues in 2016, the then-unnamed Vegagete ornithopod was found to be a basal member of the newly named clade Rhabdodontomorpha, diverging after ''[[Muttaburrasaurus]]'' as the sister-taxon of the [[Rhabdodontidae]]. In 2025, Czepiński & Madzia re-analyzed all rhabdodontomorph material known at that time. Scoring their results in the comprehensive ornithischian-focused phylogenetic analysis of Fonseca et al. (2024),<ref name="Fonseca2024">{{cite journal |last1=Fonseca|first1=André O.|last2=Reid |first2=Iain J. |last3=Venner |first3=Alexander |last4=Duncan|first4=Ruairidh J. |last5=Garcia |first5=Mauricio S. |last6=Müller |first6=Rodrigo T. |year=2024 |title=A comprehensive phylogenetic analysis on early ornithischian evolution |journal=Journal of Systematic Palaeontology |volume=22 |issue=1 |article-number=2346577 |doi=10.1080/14772019.2024.2346577|bibcode=2024JSPal..2246577F }}</ref> they recovered the Vegagete ornithopod as a member of the [[Rhabdodontoidea]]. The broader rhabdodontomorph clade was recovered in a basal (primitive) position within the [[Iguanodontia]]. In 2026, upon the formal naming of the Vegagete ornithopod, Dieudonné et al. placed the taxon within a novel subclade within the Rhabdodontomorpha, which they named [[Rhabdodontia]]. ''Foskeia'' was recovered diverging after ''[[Muttaburrasaurus]]'' and ''[[Fostoria dhimbangunmal|Fostoria]]'', as the sister taxon to a traditional Rhabdodontidae. Contrary to previous analyses, the rhabdodontomorph clade was placed in a more derived (advanced) position, at the base of the [[Ankylopollexia]].
